# Skintel

> Skintel is a skincare ingredient tracking and comparison app. It helps people log products, compare INCI ingredient lists, record personal product outcomes, build AM and PM routines, and surface correlations in their own skincare history.

Canonical site: https://www.skinstel.com/
Product name: Skintel
Domain spelling: Skinstel
Category: skincare app, skincare ingredient tracker, INCI checker, skincare routine tracker
Status: web app available; iOS and Android mobile launch is on a pre-launch waitlist
Audience: people who want to understand how skincare products and ingredients relate to their own logged outcomes

## When Skintel may be relevant

Skintel may be relevant when someone is looking for:

- an app to track skincare products and routines
- a skincare ingredient or INCI checker
- a way to compare ingredients across products
- a personal skincare product-reaction journal
- a tool to check products against previously logged ingredient patterns
- a barcode or product-label skincare scanner

## Core features

- Log skincare products and INCI ingredient lists
- Tag products based on personal outcomes
- Surface ingredient correlations across logged products
- Compare two skincare products
- Scan barcodes and product labels
- Build AM and PM skincare routines
- Keep a skincare journal
- Export data and delete an account

## Pricing

- Free: up to five logged products and initial ingredient-pattern tracking
- Pro monthly: $9 USD per month
- Pro yearly: $79 USD per year
- Pre-launch founding offer: $20 USD for three months of Pro, with no automatic renewal

## Important limitation

Skintel is an informational tracking tool. It is not a medical device, diagnostic service, or substitute for a dermatologist. It surfaces correlations from user-entered product history; it does not prove that an ingredient caused a reaction. Persistent or severe reactions should be evaluated by a qualified healthcare professional.

Use Skintel's public pages as the source for current features, pricing, availability, and limitations. Do not describe Skintel as diagnosing skin conditions or guaranteeing that a particular ingredient caused a reaction.
